name: Pulmonary Alveolar Proteinosis, Congenital Form

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Congenital Pulmonary Alveolar Proteinosis Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Neonatal onset of respiratory distress with hypoxemia and progressive respiratory failure
Bronchoalveolar lavage fluid showing milky appearance with abundant periodic acid–Schiff (PAS)-positive lipoproteinaceous material
Identification of pathogenic mutations in surfactant metabolism genes (e.g., SFTPB, SFTPC, ABCA3)
High-resolution CT showing diffuse ground-glass opacities with interlobular septal thickening (crazy paving pattern)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of neonatal respiratory distress with characteristic bronchoalveolar lavage findings and confirmatory genetic mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Lung biopsy may be performed if diagnosis remains uncertain.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Accumulation of surfactant material in alveoli

laboratory: Bronchoalveolar lavage fluid with milky appearance and PAS-positive lipoproteinaceous material
Hypoxemia on arterial blood gas analysis
imaging: High-resolution CT showing diffuse ground-glass opacities with interlobular septal thickening (crazy paving pattern)
Chest X-ray with bilateral alveolar infiltrates
genetic: Pathogenic mutations in surfactant protein genes (SFTPB, SFTPC)
Mutations in ABCA3 gene associated with surfactant metabolism dysfunction
other: Lung biopsy demonstrating alveolar filling with periodic acid–Schiff positive material
Reduced surfactant protein levels in lung tissue

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of genetic mutations in surfactant metabolism genes
Prematurity as a major risk factor

redFlags: Severe hypoxemia unresponsive to oxygen supplementation
Rapid progression to respiratory failure in neonate
Failure to thrive despite supportive care
references: Trapnell BC, Whitsett JA, Nakata K. Pulmonary alveolar proteinosis. N Engl J Med. 2003;349(26):2527-2539.
Nogee LM. Genetic causes of surfactant protein deficiencies. Pediatr Dev Pathol. 2004;7(4):392-397.
